column1: # clues.tsv for do_op — pedagogic hints only. NEVER state expected output, messages, or the fix.
# do_op is a PROGRAM: it owns main and reads its inputs from argv, so there is no labeled case list.
# Single member-less foothold hint: fires on ANY failing case.

do_op is run as a program, so its three pieces of input arrive as text in argv, not from scanf — which slots of argv hold the two numbers and which holds the operator? Each number is a string of characters you have to turn into an integer yourself, the same way an atoi-style walk does. Before you touch argv at all, ask how many arguments you were actually given: what should happen when there are too few or too many? Then think about the operator: you only know how to handle a small set of symbols — what do you do with anything else? And two of those operations have an input that is forbidden — which divisor turns a divide or a remainder into something the machine refuses to compute, and how do you check for it before performing the operation rather than after crashing?
